chart.description: Displays a chart (lines, bars or pie) in the AgentUI chat. Use it to illustrate numeric data; accompany it with a sentence of explanation. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

kind.description: line = trend, bar = comparison, pie = breakdown (a single series).

y.description: As many numbers as labels in x.

map.description: Locates 1 to 10 places on an OpenStreetMap map in the AgentUI chat. Only give coordinates you are sure about. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

maps.description: Adds a global "Open in Maps" button (place page, or route in point order).

text.description: Markdown displayed in the point's popup.

maps.description: "Open in Maps" button on this point.

code.description: Presents a code or configuration excerpt or a diff (line numbers, highlighting, Copy button) in the AgentUI chat. Reserve it for excerpts the user will want to copy or reread. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

language.description: ts, js, python, bash, json, yaml, sql, html, css, or diff (+ / - lines).

highlight.description: Lines to highlight: numbers or ranges like "6-7".

start.description: Number of the first line (1 by default).

table.description: Displays a data table (column sorting, folding of long tables, CSV copy) in the AgentUI chat. Use it to compare several items on several criteria; accompany it with a sentence of explanation. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

unit.description: Unit displayed after each number of the column.

items.description: One value per column, in order. null = empty cell.

progress.description: Displays a checklist of steps with a progress bar for a long task (several steps, chained tools), which you update as the work goes. The component appears automatically at the top of your reply from the first call: NEVER write the token in your text. For each update, call the tool again with `update` = the token returned by the first call and the COMPLETE state of all steps; the component changes in place. Set the current step to `running`, finish it with `done` (or `failed`) before moving to the next. Create only one per task; pointless for a short task.

detail.description: Short note displayed under the step (progress, error…).

update.description: [[agentui:…]] token returned by the first call, to update this component instead of creating another one.

image.description: Displays one or more images (gallery with full-screen viewer) in the AgentUI chat. `src`: an https://… URL OR an absolute path of a file on your machine (png, jpeg, gif or webp, 20 MB max) that the plugin copies and serves to the user; use neither data: nor file:. Caption per image is optional. Accompany the images with a sentence of explanation. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

src.description: https://… URL or absolute path of an image file on your machine.

custom.description: Displays a dynamic, interactive widget in the AgentUI chat, written as a React component with the same UI kit as the miniapps. Use it when a static chart/table/map is not enough and the user should play with the result: calculator or simulator with sliders, filterable list, converter, quiz, timer, mini-dashboard, form with live preview. It is NOT persistent and has no backend or storage (state lives in the component, lost on reload); for something the user will keep using, create a miniapp instead (agentui_miniapp_guide). `code` is ONE TSX module that default-exports the component (React 18, automatic JSX: no need to import React; hooks from 'react'). The only importable modules are 'react', '@agentui/ui', 'chart.js' and 'leaflet' (interactive maps: `import L from 'leaflet'`, its CSS is preloaded; use OpenStreetMap tiles https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png (served through AgentUI) with attribution, create the map in a useEffect on a ref'd div with an explicit height and call map.remove() on cleanup); no relative imports, no other network, no fetch. @agentui/ui: Stack, Row (gap, align, justify, wrap), Card (padding), Text (variant: h5 h6 subtitle body caption overline; muted, mono), Divider, Button (variant: contained outlined text; color: primary danger neutral; size: small; icon; loading), IconButton (icon, label), Icon (name), TextField (value, onChange(value: string), label, type, multiline, placeholder, onEnter), Select (value, onChange, options), Checkbox/Switch (checked, onChange(boolean), label), List/ListItem (primary, secondary, leading, trailing, onClick), Table (columns: {key,label,align?,render?}[], rows), Tabs (value, onChange, tabs: {value,label}[]), Chip (label, color), Alert (severity: info success warning error), Spinner, EmptyState, Chart (type: line bar doughnut; labels; series: {name,data}[]; height), toast(message), openUrl(url), useLang(), useTheme(), reply(text) and useCanReply() (see below). Icon names: add close check delete edit search refresh back forward star heart info warning error chevron-right chevron-down send download play pause more home person apps checklist. Style with the --au-* CSS variables (var(--au-accent), var(--au-muted), var(--au-line)…) so it follows the light/dark theme; never hard-code colors. Do not use Page (it is a full-screen layout): start with Card or Stack; the widget is sized to its content. Keep it compact (it sits in a chat bubble) and show texts in the user's language. WIDTH: the widget gets the width of the chat bubble, about 250-330 px on a phone and up to ~700 px on a desktop, and anything wider is CUT on the right without a scrollbar. NEVER hard-code a width (no `width: 320`, no fixed-size canvas): use `width: '100%'` and `useWidth()` (from '@agentui/ui', width in px, updated on resize) to size a canvas or a board, keeping its aspect ratio (a fixed height is fine). Test mentally at 260 px. FULLSCREEN: for something meant to be played or read big (a game, a board, a chart), offer a button that calls `requestFullscreen()` (from '@agentui/ui', in a click handler: it is refused otherwise). The SAME component then covers the whole screen without reloading, so its state and running loop are kept; `useFullscreen()` is true meanwhile, and `useWidth()` / `useHeight()` give the screen size (height is `undefined` in the chat, where the widget is sized to its content): re-layout with them, e.g. a bigger canvas. `exitFullscreen()` closes it; the host also draws a close button and Escape closes it, so you do not need to add one. INTERACTION: `reply(text)` (from '@agentui/ui', call it in a click handler) sends `text` in the chat as the user's next message, and you answer it like any message. Use it for actions that need you: a 'Details' button that calls reply(`Give me more details about the offer: ${offer.name}`), a choice in a list, a 'Compare' or 'Book' button. Write the text as the user would say it, with everything you need to act (name, id, values), since you will not see the widget's state. It returns a Promise<boolean> (false = refused, e.g. you are still working); `useCanReply()` is false while you are working, so disable such buttons with it. Do not call reply on load or on a timer: it only works after a click in the widget. LIVE WIDGET (two-way: a game, a wizard, a live board, any exchange that stays inside the same component): an agentui_widget_custom widget becomes a live widget when you keep a session open with it (agentui_widget_custom_wait). in the component, `reply(text, { silent: true })` sends `text` to you as an EVENT over a live session (no message in the chat) and `useAgentState<T>(initial?)` (from '@agentui/ui') returns the latest `state` you pushed. Flow: (1) call agentui_widget_custom with `code` and an initial `state`, write the token in your reply; (2) call agentui_widget_custom_wait with that token: it BLOCKS until the user acts in the widget and returns the event (e.g. their chess move); (3) call agentui_widget_custom with `update` = the token and the new `state` (no `code`): the SAME widget updates in place, keeping its own React state, and do NOT write the token again; (4) call agentui_widget_custom_wait again, and so on until the exchange is over, then just stop calling it and conclude normally. `state` is any JSON value (max 32 KB, replaces the previous one entirely, so put everything the component needs in it, e.g. the full position, not only the last move). The widget must render from `useAgentState` (with a sensible `initial`) and call reply with a text that contains what you need to act (e.g. `move e2e4`). It is only live while you are in agentui_widget_custom_wait: `useCanReply()` is false (disable the board) while you think. For a plain question to the user, agentui_ask / agentui_form remain simpler. Compilation errors are shown to the user, so write valid TSX. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself. MEDIA: to show images, videos or audio of yours inside the component, list their absolute paths in `media` and render them with <Media name={path} /> (or useMedia(path)) from @agentui/ui.

code.description: The complete TSX module (max 64 KB), with `export default function Widget() { … }`. Required when creating the widget; omit it with `update`.

height.description: Maximum height in px before the widget scrolls inside the chat (default 2400, max 4000): leave it unset, the widget is sized to its content.

update.description: Token ([[agentui:…]]) of a widget already displayed: pushes `state` to it instead of creating a new one. No `code`.

state.description: JSON value (max 32 KB) given to the component through useAgentState(). With `update`, replaces the previous state.

media.description: Images, videos or audio files (absolute paths on your machine, 8 at most) the component displays. AgentUI copies them into the chat; in the code, use each path exactly as written here: `<Media name="/home/me/clip.mp4" />`, or `useMedia(path)` for `.url`. Without it the component cannot show your files (it has no network access). Only when creating the widget (not with `update`).

video.description: Displays a video player (fullscreen, speed, seeking) in the AgentUI chat. `src`: an https://… URL OR an absolute path of a video file on your machine (mp4, webm or mov; 45 MB max, H.264/AAC mp4 plays everywhere) that the plugin copies and serves to the user; use neither data: nor file:. Accompany the video with a sentence of explanation. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

src.description: https://… URL or absolute path of a video file on your machine (mp4, webm or mov, 45 MB max), which the plugin copies and serves to the user. No data:, file: or relative path.

audio.description: Displays an audio player (play/pause, seeking, speed) in the AgentUI chat: a voice note, a recording, a generated sound. `src`: an https://… URL OR an absolute path of an audio file on your machine (mp3, m4a, ogg, wav, flac, aac or webm; 45 MB max) that the plugin copies and serves to the user; use neither data: nor file:. One track per call. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

src.description: https://… URL or absolute path of an audio file on your machine (mp3, m4a, ogg, wav, flac, aac or webm, 45 MB max), which the plugin copies and serves to the user. No data:, file: or relative path.

title.description: Name shown in the player (default: the file name).

pdf.description: Displays a PDF document (page preview, full-screen reader with zoom, download) in the AgentUI chat. `src`: an https://… URL (its server must allow cross-origin reads, otherwise the user only gets a link) OR an absolute path of a PDF file on your machine (45 MB max) that the plugin copies and serves to the user; use neither data: nor file:. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

src.description: https://… URL or absolute path of a PDF file on your machine (PDF, 45 MB max), which the plugin copies and serves to the user. No data:, file: or relative path.

markdown.description: Displays a long or standalone Markdown document as a card (rendered with tables and code, collapsed beyond a dozen lines with a full-screen view, copy and download buttons): a report, notes, a README. Give exactly one of `content` (the Markdown text) and `src` (absolute path of a .md or .txt file on your machine, copied into the chat). For a normal answer, write Markdown directly in your reply instead. Returns a [[agentui:…]] token: write it as is in your reply, where the component should appear, and never write the JSON yourself.

src.description: Absolute path of a .md, .markdown or .txt file on your machine.

tokenInstruction: Place this token as is in your reply, where the component should appear.

ask.description: Asks the user a question in AgentUI (choice buttons or free answer) and waits for the answer. Use only if you really need information. The tool BLOCKS until the user answers and returns the answer as its result: write nothing else in the same turn, then continue your task based on the answer.

options.description: Proposed choices. Without options: free answer.

multiple.description: With options: the user may choose several (answer: labels separated by commas).

confirm.description: Asks the user for permission before a risky or irreversible action (two buttons) and waits for the decision. The answer is the label of the chosen button; only act after a "yes". The tool BLOCKS until the user answers and returns the answer as its result: write nothing else in the same turn, then continue your task based on the answer.

title.description: What needs to be authorized, phrased as a question.

yes.description: Label of the confirm button (default: Confirm).

no.description: Label of the cancel button (default: Cancel).

form.description: Displays a form when you need several pieces of information at once (rather than several questions) and waits for it to be submitted. The answer is one "Label: value" line per field ("Yes"/"No" for a checkbox, "—" if an optional field is empty). The tool BLOCKS until the user answers and returns the answer as its result: write nothing else in the same turn, then continue your task based on the answer.

custom_wait.description: Keeps a live session with a widget you created with agentui_widget_custom, which makes it a LIVE WIDGET (read that tool's description, section LIVE WIDGET): WAITS until the user acts in it and returns the event. The tool BLOCKS and returns {"from":"widget","widget":<token>,"event":<text the component passed to reply(text, { silent: true })>}, or {"from":"user","message":<text>} if the user typed in the chat instead, or {"timeout":true} after `timeout_s` seconds without anything (call it again to keep listening, or stop). Call it IN THE SAME TURN right after creating the widget (a widget you do not listen to is dead: its buttons stay disabled), and never create a second widget for the same exchange: reuse the first one. Loop: agentui_widget_custom_wait, then agentui_widget_custom with `update` + `state`, then agentui_widget_custom_wait again. Stop calling it to end the session (game over, wizard done): the widget is then no longer live. Everything you write ends up in the single chat message that holds the widget, so write nothing between two calls unless it is worth showing.

widget.description: The widget's [[agentui:…]] id, exactly as returned by agentui_widget_custom.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for an event (default 600, max 1800).

updateInstruction: Update applied: the displayed component has changed. Do not write the token.
progressInstruction: The component is already displayed in the chat: do not write this token in your reply. To update it, call the tool again with update = this token and the complete state of the steps.

guide.description: Returns the guide for building AgentUI miniapps (React front + handlers, shown in the Miniapps tab): file layout, UI components, CSS variables, backend API, rules. READ IT BEFORE creating or modifying a miniapp.

create.description: Creates (or renames) a miniapp shown in the Miniapps tab of AgentUI. Then send its files with agentui_miniapp_write. Call agentui_miniapp_guide first if you have not read the guide.

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

name.description: Name displayed in the Miniapps tab.

icon.description: Icon name from the guide (default: apps).

fs.description: Files/folders the miniapp's handlers (ctx.fs) may access, declared once here. Absolute paths, under the folders the administrator allows. Each grant stays inactive until the user approves it in the miniapp header. Re-sending replaces the list.

path.description: Absolute path of a folder (covers its content) or of one file.

write.description: Writes files of a miniapp (created or replaced) then builds it. Paths: src/main.tsx (required, default-exports the root React component), other src/** modules, and server/<route>.js for the handlers (server side). Returns {ok:true} or {ok:false, errors:[{file,line,message}]}: on errors, fix and write again (the previous working version stays online).

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

read.description: Reads a file of one of your miniapps.

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

list.description: Lists your miniapps with their files.

delete_file.description: Deletes a file of one of your miniapps then rebuilds it.

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

remove.description: Permanently deletes a miniapp with its files and its data. Only on explicit request of the user (ask for confirmation with agentui_confirm first).

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

logs.description: Recent handler logs of a miniapp (console.log output, handler errors, timeouts) — use it to debug your handlers (server/*.js).

id.description: Miniapp id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 2-40 characters, starting with a letter (e.g. habit-tracker).

open.description: Gives you a temporary link that opens one of your miniapps in YOUR browser tool, running for real (front, handlers and data), to check that it looks and works as the user will see it. Open it after agentui_miniapp_write, look at the page, click through it, and fix what is wrong. The page text also lists the errors of the front and the failed handler calls (#agentui-errors, and body[data-state] is loading, ready or error), so read it when something looks off; handler-side output stays in agentui_miniapp_logs. The link opens only this miniapp, needs no login, expires (15 minutes by default, 1 hour at most) and the page reloads by itself when you write a new version, so you rarely need a second link. Beware: the app is used for real, so what you click writes real data (use a test entry and remove it). Do not share the link with the user, they have the Miniapps tab.

ttl_s.description: Lifetime of the link in seconds (default 900).

job.description: Tags a scheduled task (cron job) as belonging to one of your miniapps, so AgentUI shows the link and deletes the task when the miniapp is removed. Create the task with your usual scheduler tool, then call this with action link and the task id. Use unlink to drop the tag without deleting the task, list to see the tagged task ids.

job_id.description: Id of the scheduled task (required for link / unlink).

data.description: Reads or writes the data of one of your miniapps (the same collections and key/value store its handlers see through ctx.db / ctx.kv). Use it to push data into a miniapp from outside a user request — typically from a cron job or after fetching something yourself — and to inspect what the miniapp stored. Open miniapps refresh automatically. Actions: find (collection, filter?, limit?, sort?, desc?), get (collection, doc_id), insert (collection, doc), update (collection, doc_id, doc = fields to merge), remove (collection, doc_id), kv_get / kv_delete (key), kv_set (key, value).

asset.description: Gives a miniapp an image, video or audio file from your machine (png, jpeg, gif, webp, mp4, webm, mov, mp3, m4a, ogg, wav, flac; 25 MB, 40 files per miniapp). In the front, `<Media name="<name>" />` or `useMedia(name)` from @agentui/ui shows it (the iframe cannot load anything else). Calling it again with the same name replaces the file, and open miniapps refresh. To show a media in a miniapp, always use this tool: a miniapp front cannot reach URLs or files by itself.

src.description: Absolute path of the file on your machine.

name.description: Name the front uses to refer to it (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; max 100). Default: the file name.

delete_asset.description: Removes a media file added with agentui_miniapp_asset.

notify.description: Sends a push notification to the user's devices (AgentUI installed as a PWA). Use it sparingly, to get their attention when it matters: a long task is finished, something needs their decision, an alert fired. Never for routine chat replies (AgentUI already notifies those). Returns how many devices were notified.

body.description: One or two sentences of detail.

url.description: Link opened when the user taps the notification: an AgentUI path ("/miniapps/<id>", "/c/<conversationId>") or an https:// URL. Default: the AgentUI home.

set_thread_title.description: Renames the current AgentUI discussion. The title is shown in the conversation list and in the header. Use it once the topic is clear (a discussion starts with the first words of the user's message as its title), or when the subject changes: short and descriptive, in the user's language, no quotes or emoji. Do not call it again without a reason, and do not mention it in your reply.

title.description: The new title: a few words.

get_thread_title.description: Returns the current title of the AgentUI discussion you are in ({ title }). Use it before agentui_set_thread_title to know whether the title is still the automatic one (the first words of the user's first message) or was already chosen, and to avoid renaming for nothing.

usageGuide:
You are chatting through AgentUI, a web chat that renders Markdown and rich components. Prefer its tools over plain text whenever they fit; do not announce them, just use them:
- agentui_widget_chart: numeric series or trends (line, bar, pie) instead of listing numbers.
- agentui_widget_table: comparing several items on several criteria, instead of a Markdown table.
- agentui_widget_map: any place or route you can locate with certainty.
- agentui_widget_code: a code, config or diff excerpt the user will copy or reread.
- agentui_widget_image: showing images or screenshots (URL or local file).
- agentui_widget_video / agentui_widget_audio / agentui_widget_pdf: a video, a voice note or sound, a PDF document (URL or local file).
- agentui_widget_markdown: a long document or report as a card (inline content or a .md file).
Files you attach with MEDIA:/path are shown automatically in the matching player: no tool needed for those.
- agentui_widget_progress: a long task with several steps, updated as you go.
- agentui_confirm: BEFORE any sensitive or irreversible action (deleting, sending, paying, overwriting).
- agentui_ask / agentui_form: whenever you need an answer or several inputs from the user; never ask them as plain text.
- agentui_widget_custom: a one-off interactive component (simulator, converter, filterable list, quiz) written as a React component. For a back-and-forth with the user inside the same component (chess, wizard), make it a live widget: keep a session open with agentui_widget_custom_wait for the user's action, then agentui_widget_custom with `update` + `state`, in a loop.
- agentui_miniapp_guide then agentui_miniapp_*: a persistent tool the user will keep using (tracker, dashboard, list).
- agentui_notify: a push notification when a long task finishes or something needs attention while the user is away.
- agentui_set_thread_title: give the discussion a short, descriptive title once its topic is clear, or when it changes; agentui_get_thread_title reads the current one first. Do not mention them.
Display tools return a [[agentui:…]] token: write it in your reply where the component should appear.
